notes:
Inbound SMB lead via self-serve signup (trial credits used). Wants hosted API, public cloud — no Private/Dedicated right now. Main ask: model selection guidance for production chat/FAQ assistant that balances cost and answer quality. Team is engineering-led but product owner (Lina — quoted) will make final decision.

Key quotes:
- "Need the cheapest model that doesn't degrade answer quality below our CS baseline." — Lina (product)
- "We expect 20–25 concurrent users initially; scale to 200 after Q3 if good." — Eng mgr

Initial technical requirements (from call 2026-02-28):
- Workloads: chat + doc search embeddings for retrieval-augmented responses; summarization for long threads.
- Latency target: median generation latency <300ms for short replies, 95th <700ms for longer; burstable throughput 30 req/s for short prompts.
- Cost sensitivity: want to keep hosted API spend < $2k/mo during POC.
- Preferred models to evaluate: Llama family quantized variants (cheap, smaller), Mistral variants (good instruction tuning), Qwen (multilingual/codex-like strengths).
- Routing: prefer single-model + fallback to smaller cheaper variant on cost events. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.

Security/compliance notes:
- SMB, but requires SSO (SAML) integration with Okta for admin console access. Audit logs required for customer-facing changes. No immediate on-prem or air-gapped need. Data residency: prefers NA but will ask about EU for some clients.

POC plan discussed:
- AE/SE to run 3-way comparison on 500-sample prompt set (mix of FAQs, long docs, code snippets). Metrics: helpfulness, hallucination rate, token cost, average latency.
- Deliverable: short report + per-model cost/profile matrix and recommended default for production.

CRM next actions (short):
- Sophie (AE) to send calendar invite + attach prompt set (by 2026-03-11).
- Daniel (SE) to prepare cost estimate + quick benchmark script and instructions for self-serve test (by 2026-03-14).
- Follow-up call to review results and discuss rollout path (canary vs immediate cutover).
